original_question: Is the chromosome where the gene that is mutated in Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva is located an autosome?

final_qi.question: Is the chromosome where the gene that is mutated in Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva is located an autosome?
final_qi.long_answer: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is almost always caused by heterozygous activating mutations in the ACVR1 gene (also called ALK2). This gene is mapped to chromosome 2q23-24. Chromosome 2 is one of the 22 numbered human chromosomes that are autosomes (i.e., not the sex chromosomes X or Y). Therefore, the chromosome on which the disease-causing gene resides is indeed an autosome.
